Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

Today we are going to explore one of the most powerful features of Python, which is modules.

Key details

  • Modules help us write a clean, organized and reusable code and then play a major role in real-world software development.
  • A module is simply a Python file that contains code functions, classes, or variables.
  • That we can reuse them in other programs.
  • Python already gives us many built-in modules like math.
  • OS, random and date and time, etc.
  • That makes our life easier.
  • And the best part is we can create our own modules.
  • We can create our own modules and even we have third party modules.
  • What are the advantages of modules?
  • Why do we use modules?
  • First one is reusability.
  • You write the code once and use it again and again.
  • This saves a huge amount of time.
  • Instead of writing code one, writing one long program, we break into smaller parts.
  • Each part becomes easier to develop and debug.
  • Next comes separate namespaces.
  • Every module has its own space for names.
  • Better organization, modul us structure a project neatly, especially when it grows larger.
  • In short, modules makes our programs cleaner, smarter, and scalable.
  • Next comes types of modules.
  • We have three types built-in modules, user defined modules, and third party modules.
  • Pip is a command to install packages.
  • This is a tool to install and manage the third party Python packages.
  • Then if you want to uninstall the module, you can give pip uninstall and the module name.
  • And if you want to see what are the modules that you have installed.
  • PIP list gives you a view of what all modules that you have installed.
  • Almost every advanced Python project uses PIP.
  • Next one is.
  • We'll talk about the types of modules.
  • Built-in modules.
  • Built-in modules come packaged with Python.
  • You don't need to install anything, just import them and use them.
  • These modules for everyday programming needs.
  • Next comes built-in modules, ways to import the built-in modules.
  • and the module name.
  • Import specific attributes.
  • From math import square root.
  • It is enough if you use square root, the just the function name.
  • And in this case,.
  • When you are importing specific attributes, you can only use those specific ones which you have imported, not all of them.
  • Importing all from math import start.
  • This is not recommended.
  • If you don't if the specific attributes or specific functions, please import only them, not import star.
  • Then next one is user defined modules.
  • Whenever we write a Python file with some useful functions and save it as.py file, that can be imported to another program.
  • This is an excellent way to organize your own function and reuse them across projects.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let's look at the advantages.
  • Let's go deeper into each of these types.
  • Before that, let's see what is pip.

  • Finally we have third party modules.
  • These are created by Python community and gives us advanced capabilities.
